sources.entry: Wishlist - Wishlist application that you can share with your friends and family. MIT Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Wishlist is a self-hosted wishlist application that you share with friends and family so they can see and claim gift items.
summary.what_it_does: Wishlist lets users create wishlists, add items manually or by fetching product data from a URL, and share them with others. Visitors can claim items, and owners can check off claimed items as purchased. It supports multiple groups (for example, friends and family), each with separate wishes and group managers. A Registry Mode turns a group into a single public list that people can claim from without signing in. Suggestions can be made on another person's list with approval, auto-approval, or a hidden "Surprise Me" mode. Authentication options include email invites over SMTP, OAuth via OpenID Connect, and proxy/header authentication. A bookmarklet can add items from product pages.
use_cases: share a gift wishlist with family for holidays
let friends claim gifts so nobody buys duplicates
create a public wedding or baby registry
track purchased gifts on a shared list
self-host a wish list for a group of friends
add products to a wishlist from a web page using a bookmarklet
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yaml file using the image ghcr.io/cmintey/wishlist:latest, mapping port 3280 and volumes for ./uploads and ./data.
Set the ORIGIN environment variable to the URL users will connect to (include the port if using an IP address).
Optionally set TOKEN_TIME, DEFAULT_CURRENCY, and MAX_IMAGE_SIZE environment variables.
Open http://<host>:3280 and complete the setup wizard to create the first user.
notable: Registry Mode: a single-list public link where visitors claim items without an account
Suggestion modes including a hidden 'Surprise Me' mode where the recipient cannot see the item
Multiple groups with separate wishes and group manager roles
Bookmarklet that opens Wishlist with the current product URL pre-filled
PWA support and OAuth login via any OpenID Connect provider
caveats: Proxy/header authentication is unsafe if the reverse proxy is misconfigured, since forged headers could grant access
Wishlist does not support running on a different URL subpath; it is recommended to run behind a reverse proxy
Nginx and Synology NAS proxies need specific buffer settings to avoid a known issue
Registry Mode claims cannot be un-claimed
